content divided into stacked horizontal zones/registers
justification: Both surfaces show a human figure with an outstretched arm grasping something (a raised staff or weapon in A, reins in B) alongside a profile quadruped, and both distribute content in stacked horizontal zones, but these are near-universal motifs. The decisive differences are in depiction and combination: A is radically schematic (stick-limbed body, a boat with a row of identical crew strokes, an isolated stylised animal), while B is naturalistic and anatomically detailed, showing a man in direct contact with a bridled horse — a specific groom-and-horse scene absent from A.
